title: Sort regular and irregular polygons by side lengths and angles

lesson.title: Regular or Not? Let's Sort Polygons!

steps.say: You already know how to spot a polygon and name it by its sides — a shape with four straight sides is a quadrilateral, three sides is a triangle. Today we learn one new job: deciding whether a polygon is regular or irregular. Here is the secret. A polygon is regular only when ALL its sides are the same length AND all its corners are the same size. Both things, together.

Let's look at a square floor tile from a Vancouver kitchen. Every side is five centimetres, and every corner is a square corner. All four sides equal, all four corners equal. So this square is a regular polygon. It gets a big yes.

visual.caption: Square tile: 5 cm on every side, all corners equal — REGULAR

steps.say: Now here is the tricky one, and this is where lots of kids slip. Look at a rectangle door mat that is eight centimetres long and three centimetres wide. It looks so neat and tidy that many children shout regular! But check the sides. Eight is not the same as three. The sides are not all equal, so this rectangle is irregular — even though all four corners are square corners. Neat-looking is not the test. Both sides and angles must match.

visual.caption: Rectangle mat: 8 cm and 3 cm sides — corners equal, sides NOT equal — IRREGULAR

steps.say: Let's sort a triangle the same careful way. Here is a triangle with a base of six centimetres and a height of four centimetres. Its three sides are six, five, and five centimetres. Six does not equal five, so the sides are not all the same. Irregular. A triangle is only regular when all three sides match and all three corners match — that one is called an equilateral triangle.

visual.caption: Sides 6 cm, 5 cm, 5 cm — not all equal — IRREGULAR

steps.say: So here is your two-question checklist for any polygon. Question one: are all the sides the same length? Question two: are all the angles the same size? Two yeses means regular. Even one no means irregular. Try it out loud on the square: yes and yes, regular. On the rectangle: no and yes, irregular.

visual.caption: Two yeses: 4 cm on every side, equal corners — REGULAR

steps.say: Remember this and you will never be tricked again. A polygon is regular only when every side is equal AND every angle is equal — a rectangle that is not a square is irregular, no matter how tidy it looks.

lesson.answer: Regular means BOTH: all sides equal AND all angles equal. Only one of the two? Then it's irregular.

practice.question: Ms. Yuanyuan tapes two shapes on the whiteboard. Shape A is a rectangle poster that is 9 centimetres long and 9 centimetres wide, with four square corners. Shape B is a rectangle bookmark that is 10 centimetres long and 2 centimetres wide, also with four square corners. Which one is regular, which one is irregular, and how do you know?
practice.answer: Shape A is regular: all four sides are 9 centimetres and all four corners are equal — both checks say yes. Shape B is irregular: its corners are all equal, but 10 centimetres is not the same as 2 centimetres, so the sides are not all equal. One 'no' is enough to make it irregular.
